tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: GPT-6.1 Terra Codex model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

Implement a chat-first UI redesign in this isolated worktree. The main session is separately improving reconstruction and refinement reliability. Keep those efforts independent, agree on shared interfaces, and do not duplicate or rewrite its pipelines.

Use planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation and independent implementation review. Reviewers must directly interact with the browser. Make focused commits; do not push or modify the other worktree.

Read AGENTS.md and the current product, source-first, reconstruction and handoff documentation before implementation.

### Product direction

Create a minimal interface using the actual light and dark colour schemes from my Chronicle project. Locate its theme files; if unavailable, ask for their location rather than inventing an approximation.

Initially, show a clean chat interface with blueprint attachments. When visual inspection is requested, move chat to the left and reveal a workspace on the right.

All application operations should be accessible through conversation. Keep manual orbit, zoom and pan. Citations and compact action controls may appear inside chat; avoid separate toolbars, floor selectors and settings panels.

### Target workflow

Support this conversational sequence:

1. Upload blueprint(s).
2. Show “Reading your drawings…” while originals are saved and Gemini creates a validated interpretation.
3. Show that the drawings are ready; source-grounded QA works before 3D.
4. “Show me all windows in the 3D model.”
   - Reuse the current saved model, or invoke the existing reconstruction workflow.
   - Show progress in chat.
   - Open the workspace, highlight reliably associated modeled windows, fade other geometry and frame the selection.
5. “Show this from above.”
   - Move the camera to top-down while preserving selection.
6. “Show the windows individually.”
   - Start a tour that focuses each selected window with a useful close-up orientation.
7. “Show this window in the original blueprint.”
   - Immediately pause the tour and capture the focused object when the message is submitted.
   - Open its original page and highlight its stored evidence region.
8. “Back to the model; next window.”
   - Restore the model and continue the same tour.
9. A requested refinement uses the existing attributed-input, validation and review workflow. Accepted changes update the workspace; rejected changes retain the previous usable model and explain the outcome.

### Architecture

Maintain explicit workspace state: document/revision, view mode, selected IDs, focused ID, camera, tour position, highlighting and assumption visibility.

Use:

Message + captured workspace context → typed action → validation → existing operation → updated chat/workspace

Gemini interprets language; application code resolves and validates identities; deterministic viewer code controls selection, cameras, tours and source navigation. Do not require a VLM to rediscover the focused object from screenshots.

Distinguish navigation commands, factual questions and persistent refinements. Navigation should not unnecessarily invoke the factual QA pipeline. Ask focused clarifications for genuine ambiguity; avoid blanket confirmation steps.

Agree on a small action/result contract before dependent implementation. Own frontend presentation and viewer interaction. Coordinate any backend routing changes with the main session. Do not add a new agent runtime or parallel implementation of reconstruction, QA or persistence.

### Preserve correctness

- Keep Gemini, the provider switch, source-sufficiency gate, citations and refusals.
- Preserve original coordinates, stable IDs, revision-pinned evidence, cached models and portable IFC provenance.
- Generated geometry and display assumptions never become authoritative factual evidence.
- Keep answer highlighting and assumption visibility independently controllable through chat.
- “All modeled windows” must not imply complete extraction of every real window.
- Unresolved objects retain source evidence; never fabricate meshes, matches or tighter source regions.
- Use reliable geometry/host orientation for close-ups; label uncertain orientations appropriately.
- Preserve original labels and building-type agnosticism.
- Keep failed operations and partial models visibly distinguishable from completed, reviewed results.

### Verification and scope

Start with deterministic interaction fixtures to establish layout, navigation and interruption behavior. Clearly distinguish fixtures from real inference. Then verify the workflow against actual saved models and real backend responses.

Independent browser review must exercise both themes, chat/workspace transitions, selections, camera changes, tours, interruption with “this object,” source navigation, assumptions and recoverable failures. Use a real model with renderable windows where available; separately test unresolved objects honestly.

Reuse existing capabilities first. No new formats, models, rendering engines, photorealism or infrastructure. Explain new constraints before introducing them.

Deliver the reviewed implementation, action contract, focused commits and a handoff stating what was verified with fixtures, actual artifacts and live providers, plus remaining gaps.

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF/SVG/DXF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DWG without a validated converter, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

The active product specification is docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md, with independently reviewed checkpoints in docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md. It adds local filesystem bundles, background reconstruction reviews, reviewed QA and the existing concept renderer; these are now authorized scope. Keep the configurable reconstruction model default; Hydrogen was not adopted.

Current source-first scope is docs/SOURCE_FIRST_SPEC.md with reviewed docs/SOURCE_FIRST_PLAN.md and implemented docs/SOURCE_FIRST_CONTRACT.md. Upload saves originals and extracts interpretation; 3D is explicit. Related drawing sources share revision-pinned provenance, source-linked chat and attributed batch user inputs. Keep native IFC separate from grouped drawing sources until mixed evidence validation exists. Read docs/SOURCE_FIRST_VERIFICATION.md for actual live results and remaining fidelity gaps. Focused commits are authorized; do not push.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- Remain building-type agnostic: preserve original space labels and meaningful non-residential features. Unknown use gets neutral concept styling and explicit schematic fallbacks, never automatic residential furnishing. Separate floor plans from sections, elevations and site plans; unsupported views/features remain source-linked unresolved records without invented floors. Detailed domes/roofs are out of scope.
- Concept styling/proposals never enter reasoning evidence, source counts or IFC exports. Inspection/concept use the same saved revision. Original sources and usable revisions survive operational failure, stop and restart.
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.
# First slice

The active product implementation is now specified in [PRODUCT_SPEC.md](PRODUCT_SPEC.md) and independently reviewed in [PRODUCT_PLAN.md](PRODUCT_PLAN.md). Those documents supersede the historical persistence/background/review exclusions below. The source-grounding invariants remain.

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Historical initial slice. The user's later 3D request is implemented under [3D_PLAN.md](3D_PLAN.md) and [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md); those supersede the CAD/3D exclusions below. Core provider and evidence rules remain in force.

Local-first single-process app. JPG/PNG and small PDFs are mandatory. FastAPI serves static UI and API. Render PDF pages with PDFium and send the rendered source images to Gemini/Decisions; always identify inspected pages. Persist bounded uploads only in ignored local runtime storage. No reference-building retrieval, CAD, 3D, auth, streaming, hosting or infrastructure expansion.

Authorized development exception: select the temporary OpenAI Responses adapter via AI_PROVIDER=openai while Gemini access is pending. It uses one structured sufficiency classification without a confidence score. The final sponsor demo uses AI_PROVIDER=gemini and native Gemini Decisions. All evidence and retry rules are shared; no automatic failover.

1. Bootstrap environment and establish API contract.
2. Independent plan/reliability review.
3. Backend: upload normalization, provenance, Gemini provider adapter, one sufficiency decision, one bounded unclear inspection, evidence-linked structured answers.
4. Frontend: source viewer, upload, ask, status, result/citation highlighting and clear operational errors.
5. Integration and independent implementation review; meaningful tests for unsupported answers, unclear handling, missing credentials, bad uploads, citation bounds and API failures.
6. Document and run the local workflow; live Gemini smoke test only when a Gemini credential is configured. No substitute provider without agreement.

The initial evidence gate is an experiment, not a correctness guarantee. Evaluate against standard Gemini using coverage, error among answered questions, unsupported answers, unnecessary abstention, latency and usage. Synthetic fixtures verify control flow, not model quality.
# API contract v1

## Progressive product extension

The active scope and shared contracts are [PRODUCT_SPEC.md](PRODUCT_SPEC.md) and [PRODUCT_PLAN.md](PRODUCT_PLAN.md). Existing source/scene/download routes remain compatible; `/api/ask` remains a synchronous reviewed-answer route. The browser uses these additions:

- Upload returns `building_id`, `revision_id`, monotonic `revision_number`, `review_status`, `has_scene`, `unresolved_views` and `is_new_upload`. Building identity is a SHA-256 of original uploaded bytes. Only genuinely new drawing uploads automatically start a job in the UI; reopening/reuploading does not start inference.
- `GET /api/buildings` returns `{buildings:[document_public]}`. `GET /api/buildings/{id}` returns that public record plus saved jobs, newest first.
- `POST /api/buildings/{id}/reconstruction` accepts `{base_revision_id,mode:"refine"|"reconstruct"}` and returns a job with HTTP202. Genuine native IFC is never automatically reconstructed. Existing usable models require local/source replacement checks before publication; fresh supported sources publish an early preview.
- `POST /api/questions` accepts `{document_id,question,revision_id?,request_id?}` and returns HTTP202 with a revision-pinned job. `GET /api/jobs/{id}` reports persisted progress and, after successful QA, `answer`. `POST /api/jobs/{id}/stop` prevents late publication; an in-flight provider call may still finish.
- Jobs distinguish queued/running/complete/needs_attention/failed/budget_exhausted/stopped/interrupted. API or schema failures never become source insufficiency. A failed correction leaves the usable revision intact.
- `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/evidence/{object_id}` returns a faithful native IFC record plus coverage for that exact saved revision, including non-rendered semantic records. Drawing-derived IFC is rejected on this native evidence path and continues to use original page regions.
- Answers add `building_id`, `answered_revision_id`, `display_revision_id`, support-review metadata and source-bound calculation results. Highlights are revalidated after concurrent reconstruction; original citations survive missing mappings.
- Portable artifact v4 preserves exact description, server-owned identities/tombstones and source frames. V2/V3 remain readable. Ordinary bbox changes cannot move frames; supported calibration/orientation changes require explicit evidence-backed updates. Concept proposals never enter these artifacts or reasoning records.

Below is the historical initial API contract; the extension above supersedes temporary-session and pre-review behavior.

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```
`bbox` is [left,top,right,bottom], normalized 0–1 in the original displayed page. Validate positive area and page existence. Proposal if present: `{text, basis:"explicit_assumption|reference",reference:null|string}`. No invented reference buildings. Model-generated evidence is an aid to inspection, not a verified detection guarantee. Scores are model signals, not probabilities of factual correctness. `gate.confidence` is nullable: OpenAI's temporary structured classification returns null instead of inventing a confidence score.

Provider selection: `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`, default gemini. Health additionally returns `provider`, `provider_label`, `credential_env`, `gate_kind` (`gemini_decisions|structured_classification`). For OpenAI, `decision_model` is the same configured `OPENAI_MODEL` used to generate the three-way classification. Missing/invalid configuration fails explicitly; no automatic fallback. The final demo must select Gemini.

## Provider orchestration
One overall Decisions choice on source pages + question. `unclear` allows one bounded targeted second inspection (a real crop/higher-resolution source view), then rerun the same gate with expanded evidence. Do not re-ask identical input and call it inspection. Standard Gemini explains limitations or generates a structured answer against original sources; never turn a negative gate into a factual answer. A positive gate does not force an answer when generation reveals missing evidence. Answer citations must validate; absent/invalid evidence cannot be silently accepted. Operational errors never silently fall back to a different gate/provider. No hidden live mocks or fixtures.

Provider documentation verified 2026-11-14: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api ; Python SDK requires >=3.2 for Decisions. REST endpoint https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions. Latest selected stable answer model: gemini-3.8-flash, configurable. SDK/REST details must be verified, not invented.

Implementation bound: at most two gate calls, one crop-selection call and one answer/explanation call. The crop is appended to the original pages with its original coordinates; it is not a separate source. The answer generator may downgrade a sufficient gate, never promote an insufficient/unclear gate. Arithmetic uses a small internal schema (sum, product, difference, quotient with source-indexed operands); code computes the value. Operand interpretation and unit compatibility still require human inspection. No claim of geometric or semantic verification is implied.
# Consolidation checkpoint — 2026-11-14

Work is on `blueprint-qa-isolated`; focused commits are local only. Read [CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md](CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md) and [CONSOLIDATION_RESULTS.md](CONSOLIDATION_RESULTS.md) for the current diagnostic evidence and acceptance gaps. - `POST /api/questions` accepts `{document_id,question,revision_id?,request_id?}` and returns HTTP202 with a revision-pinned job. `GET /api/jobs/{id}` reports persisted progress and, after successful QA, `answer`. `POST /api/jobs/{id}/stop` prevents late publication; an in-flight provider call may still finish.

- `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/evidence/{object_id}` returns a faithful native IFC record plus coverage for that exact saved revision, including non-rendered semantic records. Drawing-derived IFC is rejected on this native evidence path and continues to use original page regions.
- Answers add `building_id`, `answered_revision_id`, `display_revision_id`, support-review metadata and source-bound calculation results. Highlights are revalidated after concurrent reconstruction; original citations survive missing mappings.
- Portable artifact v4 preserves exact description, server-owned identities/tombstones and source frames. V2/V3 remain readable. Ordinary bbox changes cannot move frames; supported calibration/orientation changes require explicit evidence-backed updates. Concept proposals never enter these artifacts or reasoning records.

Below is the historical initial API contract; the extension above supersedes temporary-session and pre-review behavior.

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```
`bbox` is [left,top,right,bottom], normalized 0–1 in the original displayed page. Validate positive area and page existence. Proposal if present: `{text, basis:"explicit_assumption|reference",reference:null|string}`. No invented reference buildings. Model-generated evidence is an aid to inspection, not a verified detection guarantee. Scores are model signals, not probabilities of factual correctness. `gate.confidence` is nullable: OpenAI's temporary structured classification returns null instead of inventing a confidence score.

Provider selection: `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`, default gemini. Health additionally returns `provider`, `provider_label`, `credential_env`, `gate_kind` (`gemini_decisions|structured_classification`). For OpenAI, `decision_model` is the same configured `OPENAI_MODEL` used to generate the three-way classification. Missing/invalid configuration fails explicitly; no automatic fallback. The final demo must select Gemini.

## Provider orchestration
One overall Decisions choice on source pages + question. `unclear` allows one bounded targeted second inspection (a real crop/higher-resolution source view), then rerun the same gate with expanded evidence. Do not re-ask identical input and call it inspection. Standard Gemini explains limitations or generates a structured answer against original sources; never turn a negative gate into a factual answer. A positive gate does not force an answer when generation reveals missing evidence. Answer citations must validate; absent/invalid evidence cannot be silently accepted. Operational errors never silently fall back to a different gate/provider. No hidden live mocks or fixtures.

Provider documentation verified 2026-11-14: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api ; Python SDK requires >=3.2 for Decisions. REST endpoint https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions. Latest selected stable answer model: gemini-3.8-flash, configurable. SDK/REST details must be verified, not invented.

Implementation bound: at most two gate calls, one crop-selection call and one answer/explanation call. The crop is appended to the original pages with its original coordinates; it is not a separate source. The answer generator may downgrade a sufficient gate, never promote an insufficient/unclear gate. Arithmetic uses a small internal schema (sum, product, difference, quotient with source-indexed operands); code computes the value. Operand interpretation and unit compatibility still require human inspection. No claim of geometric or semantic verification is implied.

# V3: explicit boundaries, visible features and source comparison

Independently reviewed plan; review resolutions are in RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. Concrete shared fields are owned by root in `docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md`; that contract governs implementation. Preserve the existing original-drawing → Gemini description → deterministic IfcOpenShell → generated IFC → Three.js pipeline, portable source provenance, source-based QA, caching and stable selections. The user's new scope includes every meaningful depicted building/furnishing feature as reconstructed geometry, a labeled schematic, or an explicit unresolved source item. It does not mean reproducing every annotation or decorative line.

## Diagnosis grounded in the saved final artifacts

Inspected the unchanged original `colorful-11397.png`, `/tmp/junction-live-v2-final/colorful-11397.png.ifc`, its matching scene JSON and the saved viewer image. The final IFC and scene agree: two storeys, 11 spaces, 57 walls, one door, no windows, and no stairs/furnishing elements. Every scene element has a mesh. Two terrace/balcony spaces are represented as ordinary rooms with ten automatically generated perimeter walls. These are actual IFC modeling/description limitations, not missing viewer meshes.

The current generator turns every retained room polygon edge into a wall. Room polygons describe usable spaces, not a structural wall inventory: this invents enclosure on outdoor edges, can duplicate shared boundaries and can turn a mistaken door-leaf/arc-shaped room boundary into a wall. In the inspected final artifact the diagonal wall centerlines are on the exterior-space outlines; we have not established that this exact run traced a door leaf. The design nevertheless permits that failure and must stop deriving walls from room perimeters.

The schema cannot represent indoor/outdoor distinctions, independent boundaries, stairs, tables, cabinets or sanitary objects. The current prompt requests only selected openings, and opening hosts depend on retained room-edge indices; invalid/omitted room polygons can therefore remove otherwise visible openings. Some failed openings are summarized only as a count. The result cannot account for meaningful unrendered features individually.

The separate `/tmp/medium-quality-description.json` is another run: two floor records, 12 room records and four opening records. It is useful evidence of extraction coverage, but cannot explain individual omissions or geometry in the final IFC above. The saved final `1794` artifact has six spaces, 30 walls, five doors and two windows; use it as a regression baseline, not a ground-truth inventory.

## Narrow description changes (root finalizes contract)

Keep named x/y and left/top/right/bottom on the wire, original-page coordinates internally, existing floor regions/transforms/calibration/alignment/measurements, and medium reconstruction reasoning unless controlled live evidence warrants another choice. Extend each floor with the following compact records; no new arbitrary list caps.

- `rooms`: retain label/polygon/basis/note; add `environment: indoor|outdoor|unknown`. These produce footprint plates only. Unknown classification remains visible; it does not authorize enclosure. A terrace/balcony footprint is allowed without known elevation, floor thickness or railing height.
- `boundaries`: local stable `key`, `kind: wall|railing|open_edge`, label, original-page segment, source region, `thickness_segment` (empty if unknown), basis and concise note. One record per physical segment, shared by neighbouring spaces. Trace the depicted wall/railing itself; never door leaves, swing arcs, furniture edges or inferred room rectangles. Keep width/extrusion as current explicit display assumptions unless a valid thickness segment supplies depicted width. An open edge is recorded as open; it must not produce a wall.
- `openings`: retain door/window kind, label, original segment, source region and basis/note; replace `host_room/host_edge` with `host_wall: boundary key|null`. The host must be the correct same-floor explicit wall. Missing/ambiguous hosting is unresolved, not a guessed nearest wall. Unknown height/sill is compatible with a schematic opening and an explicit display assumption.
- `features`: `kind: stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other`, label, source region, polygon, basis and note. Source polygons may be approximate footprint symbols; unresolved geometry belongs in the unresolved list. Do not discard a visible object solely because its vertical dimensions are unknown. Stairs may be a low schematic footprint/tread indication; do not infer an actual rise, direction or connection between floors. Distinguish object geometry from the walls that surround it.
- `unresolved`: label, category, original source region and reason for visible but unclassifiable features or uncertain geometry. Server validation failures must produce equivalent persistent outcomes, not disappear into a warning count. Avoid duplicating the same item in feature and unresolved input lists. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual source extents cannot be resolved.

Keep extraction to the existing bounded request. Ask the model to account for the meaningful depicted categories across each entire floor, including openings and furnishings, without restricting it to a few illustrative examples. Model omissions are not automatically detectable: the inventory is a reconstruction audit aid, not a certified complete list or factual count source. Meaningful feature coverage needs a source-by-source visual acceptance pass.

## Deterministic generator behavior

1. Validate spaces, boundaries, openings and features independently. Invalid room polygons must not suppress valid explicit walls or openings. Existing room conflict rules remain within each floor; do not repair polygons or infer missing structural partitions.
2. Emit footprint plates for indoor/outdoor spaces with distinct provenance/classification and viewer styling. Emit IfcWall only from explicit wall records; emit railing geometry only from explicit railing records. Open edges remain visibly open. Shared boundary IDs map to one wall. Exact repeated/reversed copies can be recognized and reported; conflicting or uncertain duplicate interpretations remain unresolved rather than arbitrarily choosing one or silently merging nearby geometry. Duplicate/conflicting local boundary keys must never resolve by array order: mark the conflicting records and dependent openings unresolved unless identity is unambiguous.
3. Attach door/window void/fill relations only to their validated wall ID. Validate original endpoints/source bbox/floor consistency and the existing host-wall-band projection. Keep actual boolean openings in the IFC, rather than painting symbols on solid walls. If hosting fails, retain that exact opening as an unresolved inventory/source item. No automatic migration to a neighbouring wall and no widening source regions to force acceptance.
4. Generate simple, visibly differentiated feature geometry. Tables/cabinets may use IfcFurnishingElement, sanitary features an appropriate supported IFC product or generic furnishing subtype, and stairs a schematic product/footprint rather than a fabricated inter-storey connector. A small set of deterministic primitives is enough; this is not an asset library or detailed furniture modeling project. Record all display heights, thicknesses and other absent dimensions as assumptions.
5. Give every extracted/validated item a persistent compressed IFC GlobalId in its floor namespace. Persist its category, source, resolution status and reason. Unresolved entries become geometry-less semantic IFC entities with matching scene records; they have no invented mesh or location beyond their valid original source region. If malformed coordinates prevent reliable localization, use the known floor region explicitly marked coarse/unlocalized; do not manufacture a precise bounding box. Stable IDs survive validation omissions, caching and download/reopen. These inventories remain explicitly derived, never authoritative building counts.

Replace “at least one room must survive” with the reviewed contract's “at least one supported renderable element”: usable explicit walls/features may survive room interpretation failure. All-unresolved results remain explicit no-3D failures; do not claim a model was built. Root should retain the extraction/unresolved diagnostic payload for inspection when possible. This changes a current invariant and must be communicated; it is not a new feature-count limit.

## Source overlay must compare the actual IFC

Root's `app/comparison.py` computes the comparison from tessellated generated IFC meshes (and actual hosted void/fill geometry when needed), transformed back through the inverse stored floor matrix to the original page. The frontend places those vectors on the unchanged source image with separate layers for boundaries, indoor/outdoor footprints, openings, schematic features and unresolved regions. The overlay must not simply redraw the model's intended polygons or bounding boxes and call that a geometry check.

A full-height wall footprint projection hides opening cuts because the lintel above an opening projects over the gap. Either use appropriate mesh cross-sections or explicitly overlay actual IFC opening/fill footprints alongside projected wall footprints, with a clear legend. Do not claim that an uncut projection proves opening correctness. Compare multiple original floor regions on the same image without applying viewer explosion or display rotation to the source. Native source clicks, floor filtering and restored embedded pages must continue to work.

The UI should make unresolved items inspectable individually: selecting one shows its original region and reason. Show concise category/status totals for navigation, labeled as reconstruction inventory, not building facts. The user can inspect broad coverage without reading a long warning paragraph or searching only a selected set of doors.

## Design constraints to explain before implementation

- Independent explicit wall extraction replaces a wrong inference, but adds description content. The current token budget may then be exhausted; token-limit/provider failures remain operational errors. Run both live originals early. - Missing physical heights do not block schematic reconstruction. Assumptions remain visible and cannot answer factual height questions. Unknown scale, orientation, registration and inter-floor elevations retain current semantics.
- Source/host/geometry checks can leave clearly visible features unresolved. They must remain in the portable inventory and overlay, with reasons. This may still block visual acceptance if major recognizable features are absent; a successful HTTP status alone is not success.
- Existing upload, IFC byte/element/triangle and response safeguards remain. Additional source-linked features increase artifact size; oversized artifacts fail explicitly rather than silently dropping features/pages.
- Schematic feature silhouettes are sufficient for this hackathon. No new file formats, hidden-floor inference, structural completeness, parametric CAD editing, photorealism, cloud rendering or extra agent runtime.

BoundaryDescription.source now uses BoundaryRegion: area or normalized positive-length line. Other PageRegion/QA contracts remain strict. ## Shared uncalibrated page scale

Uncalibrated floor transforms use a page-derived factor `10/max(page.width/page.height,1)` rather than independently normalizing each floor bbox. Floor boxes affect centering only. This preserves drawn proportions among uncalibrated diagrams on one page; it does not prove physical scale or equal drawing scales, especially for independently resized diagrams. Separate page frames remain schematic. Supported physical calibration is unchanged. New `page_extent` assumptions disclose the convention; the UI checks those markers before making the claim. Existing artifacts retain stored transforms and original IDs; no automatic migration. See FLOOR_SCALE_FIX.md.

## Depicted wall bands and schematic visibility

A supplied boundary segment is a reference line, not necessarily a centerline. A valid perpendicular thickness segment establishes signed face offsets in the aspect-correct source plane. Validate contact before display rotation; extrude between those faces. This retains depicted relative widths at unknown scale. Missing/invalid widths keep explicit display defaults. Supported band contacts form junctions without endpoint snapping or filling positive gaps.

Opening range and normal-offset checks use the same source plane and named host. Gap endpoints retain their longitudinal positions. Void and fill are centered normally within the supported band (or assumed default band), with an explicit placement assumption; voids cut the full band. A previously accepted opening outside the actual supported band is not grandfathered in.

Feature footprints and source classifications remain fallible drawing interpretations. Raised schematics improve visibility without establishing vertical measurements. Relative to the existing assumed wall height H, display heights are table .30H; chair/bed .20H; sofa/sink/toilet .25H; cabinet .50H; appliance .40H; shower/bath/stairs/other .10H. Motifs and dimensions are portable assumptions. Support symbols do not establish leg counts; chair facing and stair ascent/rise/travel direction are not inferred. New geometry must remain inside the existing footprint.

Unresolved canvas annotations are HTML source links, not IFC geometry or answer highlights. Precise source regions use the stored source transform; coarse/unlocalized records use a labeled floor badge. Annotation screen positions may be separated for legibility without changing source coordinates or exported geometry. A more elevated derived-model camera exposes interiors; native IFC camera behavior is unchanged. See SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_PLAN.md and SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_RESULTS.md.

/goal Implement and integrate the product described below: progressive, source-grounded building reconstruction; JSON-mediated building reasoning; reviewed Q&A; persistent building bundles; and the existing browser-based concept presentation layer.

Work autonomously through planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation, integration, live verification and independent implementation review. Continue beyond planning until the agreed acceptance flows work or a concrete external blocker prevents further progress.

I will be offline. Resolve routine implementation decisions using the repository instructions, existing architecture and your judgment. Communicate assumptions and tradeoffs in progress updates without turning them into approval requests. Preserve existing working behavior and keep the implementation appropriate for this hackathon.

PRODUCT CONCEPT

The product uses two source-grounded review loops: one progressively improves the building model; the other checks answers before publishing them. Both preserve original evidence, explicit uncertainty and traceable revisions.

A saved building can be reopened immediately. New drawings run through background reconstruction; questions reuse the available model and evidence.

Users can switch between:
- Inspection mode: source-associated geometry, evidence, assumptions, unresolved issues and answer highlights.
- Concept mode: an architectural presentation of the same building, with clearly distinguished styling and decorative proposals.

The core experience is:

Upload or open a building, explore its 3D interpretation, and ask questions whose answers link back to the supplied evidence.

All supported inputs expose structured building context for reasoning, while the evidence rules depend on where the information came from.

INPUT PATHS AND JSON-MEDIATED BUILDING REASONING

Implement a structured reasoning interface for genuine IFC files, drawings/PDFs and our drawing-generated IFCs.

JSON makes the information usable for Gemini and deterministic code. It must preserve provenance rather than become an unqualified replacement for the source.

Inspect and reuse existing extraction, description, source-context and artifact functionality before adding new mappings. Do not duplicate capabilities that already exist.

1. Genuine uploaded IFC → reasoning JSON

Use IfcOpenShell to extract a semantic building representation containing:
- Stable IFC GlobalIds, entity types and names.
- Storeys and supported containment relationships.
- Available properties, quantities and units.
- Opening/host and space-boundary relationships where supplied.
- Relevant geometry summaries and deterministic calculations.
- Provenance for each value: supplied property or calculated result.
- Calculation methods and contributing records where relevant.
- Extraction coverage, missing data and unresolved relationships.

Include relevant geometry-less entities in the semantic catalog. Rendering availability must not determine which records can support factual answers.

Preserve references to the original IFC records. Do not invent drawing pages, citation boxes or relationships that the IFC does not provide.

Native IFC facts describe the supplied model, not guaranteed as-built reality.

Do not require Gemini to read raw IFC text or reconstruct an existing IFC. IfcOpenShell performs extraction and supported geometry operations.

2. Drawing/PDF → interpretation JSON plus original evidence

Reuse the building description and source mappings, exposing them through the shared reasoning interface.

Gemini must retain access to original pages and relevant regions. Extracted JSON is a fallible interpretation, not a replacement for the drawing.

Keep observed information, inferred interpretations and display assumptions distinct. Generated dimensions and decorative proposals must not enter factual QA as evidence.

3. Drawing-generated IFC → restored drawing context

When reopening our generated IFC, restore its embedded description, original pages, source mappings and assumptions.

Do not treat generated properties or geometry as authoritative native-IFC evidence merely because the file format is IFC.

Recover the embedded exact description where available instead of unnecessarily reconstructing it from the generated geometry.

4. Shared reasoning interface

Define a common interface for objects, relationships, evidence references, units, provenance and coverage while retaining source-specific detail.

The native-IFC extraction schema and drawing-description schema may remain different.

Do not perform a lossy conversion of arbitrary IFC geometry into simple room polygons and wall segments just to reuse BuildingDescription.

Use common stable object references to connect reasoning records, source evidence and viewer selection.

5. Use this context throughout Q&A

Retrieve question-relevant structured records for the sufficiency gate, reasoning model and post-draft review.

For native IFC:
- Code selects relevant original records.
- Code performs supported counts and calculations.
- Gemini interprets the question and explains results.
- Answers cite the contributing original IFC records and properties.

For drawings:
- Supply the structured interpretation alongside original visual evidence.
- The reviewer must not assess an answer solely against extraction JSON or the answer model’s explanation.

Validate that retrieved context covers the question’s scope. A selected subset must not be mistaken for a complete building-wide inventory.

Unsupported or incomplete calculations must expose their missing inputs and coverage limitations rather than silently returning a complete-looking total.

Preserve source-linked highlighting through shared stable IDs. Uncertain associations retain citations without invented highlights.

BUILDING-MODEL REVIEW LOOP

The building-model loop produces an interactive preview, then improves it through targeted revisions.

For drawings, the pipeline is:

Original drawing
→ building-description JSON
→ deterministic IFC generation
→ reopened geometry
→ interactive model

Genuine uploaded IFCs use direct extraction and rendering. Do not route them through drawing reconstruction or automatically rewrite their original contents.

A reconstruction reviewer examines the original drawing, description and actual generated geometry together. JSON-only review could overlook generator errors or approve a plausible interpretation that does not match the source.

1. Generate the first description and preview.

The implementer describes depicted floors, spaces, walls, openings and meaningful features, retaining source regions and uncertainty.

Deterministic code generates and reopens the IFC. After local validation, publish the first usable model as:

“Preview · review in progress.”

Do not wait for the complete refinement loop before making a usable preview available.

2. Review against the original.

Supply full-page context, relevant crops, the description and original-coordinate overlays derived from the actual reopened IFC.

Check:
- Missing meaningful features.
- Invented walls or floors.
- Wall connectivity and relative thickness.
- Opening placement, width and wall associations.
- Indoor/outdoor boundaries and incorrect enclosure.
- Furnishing and fixture coverage.
- Unsupported dimensions and other assumptions.

The reviewer must examine actual generated geometry, not only the description or attractive concept styling.

3. Return actionable feedback.

Each issue identifies:
- The affected object or original source region.
- The discrepancy.
- Supporting source evidence.
- The proposed inspection or correction.
- Any uncertainty that prevents a confident correction.

For example:

“This boundary crosses the depicted balcony opening. Reinspect this source region and revise the boundary’s classification or extent.”

Distinguish extraction, generation and display problems. If the JSON is correct but the generator renders it incorrectly, do not distort the description to compensate.

4. Apply targeted corrections.

Patch the affected description records while preserving unrelated objects and their identities.

Unsupported or ambiguous interpretations remain unresolved. Do not casually rewrite the entire building on each iteration.

Runtime models propose description corrections. They must not generate or execute Python, raw IFC text or application-code patches.

5. Validate the candidate revision.

Regenerate and reopen the IFC, then check both the requested correction and possible regressions elsewhere.

Review what disappeared as well as what improved. A repair to a balcony must not silently remove a bathroom wall or door.

Keep the previous usable revision if generation fails or a clear regression is found.

6. Publish the update without disrupting exploration.

Prepare replacement geometry offscreen and swap the complete revision into the viewer. Do not expose a partially replaced scene.

Preserve:
- Camera position and orbit target; no automatic fit.
- Selected floor and floor separation where the floor still exists.
- Inspection/concept mode.
- Cutaway and assumption controls.
- Selected object when its identity survives.
- Stable concept decoration placements where supporting geometry is unchanged.

Revalidate answer highlights against the new revision.

If an object is removed or becomes unresolved, explain the change and retain its source evidence. Do not silently select an unrelated replacement.

If the footprint changes substantially, offer “Fit updated model” instead of moving the camera automatically.

STABLE IDENTITIES AND COORDINATES

Object identities must survive insertion and reordering.

Persistent object IDs must map consistently to IFC GlobalIds. List positions cannot serve as enduring identities.

Preserve existing imported artifact IDs and compatibility. New objects receive new IDs; deleted objects must not have their IDs reassigned to unrelated features.

Source-to-display frames must remain stable during ordinary refinement. Changing a floor’s bounding box must not recenter or rescale existing geometry.

Preserve the shared-page scale fix:
- Uncalibrated diagrams on the same page retain their relative drawn proportions.
- This does not establish physical scale or prove that independently resized diagrams use equal drawing scales.
- Relationships across different pages remain schematic unless supported.
- Supported physical calibration remains intact.

Supported calibration or orientation corrections require an explicit transform update.

Use building/revision identifiers on reconstruction updates and QA requests. Reject stale patches and stale asynchronous updates rather than allowing an older job to overwrite a newer revision.

RECONSTRUCTION STOPPING BEHAVIOR

The loop stops when:
- There are no actionable supported corrections.
- Repeated attempts make no material progress.
- The user stops the job.
- An explicitly configured execution budget is reached.

Preserve the best available revision and remaining issues.

Reviewer agreement does not justify a “verified accurate” badge. Unresolved disagreements remain visible.

A model can be available with unresolved issues. Availability and completeness are separate states.

Q&A REVIEW LOOP

The Q&A loop inspects evidence, drafts internally and reviews the answer before publication.

1. Establish the evidence context.

Capture the question and current building revision.

Retrieve relevant reasoning JSON and original evidence through the shared interface.

Keep the input distinction:
- Genuine uploaded IFC: use its actual records, relationships and supported geometry calculations.
- Image/PDF: inspect original pages alongside the structured interpretation.
- Drawing-generated IFC: continue using the original drawing as evidence, including after reopening.

Drawing-generated geometry and concept decorations do not establish factual dimensions.

2. Check evidence sufficiency.

Retain the existing Decisions gate:
- Sufficient: proceed to drafting.
- Insufficient: explain what is missing from the inspected material.
- Unclear: perform the permitted targeted inspection or request clarification; unresolved uncertainty remains explicit.

Missing information is scoped to the inspected material, not asserted to be absent everywhere.

3. Generate an internal draft.

Gemini supplies:
- The proposed answer.
- Source citations.
- Relevant calculation inputs and derivations.
- Explicit limitations.

The draft is not yet presented as the final answer.

4. Run deterministic validation.

Check source references, units and calculations.

Code performs supported native-IFC counts and geometry operations using the actual records, including relevant objects without renderable geometry.

Do not ask the model to replace deterministic counting or arithmetic where the required records and inputs are available.

5. Review the draft against the evidence.

Decisions receives:
- The user’s question.
- The draft answer.
- The original evidence or faithful extracted native-IFC records.
- Relevant structured context with provenance and coverage.
- Calculation results and relevant validation findings.

For drawings, include the necessary original visual evidence. Do not supply only the reconstruction JSON or the answer model’s explanation.

Ask one overall question:

“Does the inspected original evidence support this draft’s answer to the user’s question, including its factual claims and derivations, without treating assumptions as facts?”

Route the result:
- Supported: publish after local validation passes.
- Contradicted: reinspect the evidence and revise.
- Unsupported by inspected evidence: seek missing evidence if available; otherwise explain the limitation.
- Unclear: inspect further or return explicit uncertainty.

Do not introduce a large set of independent model vetoes. Add targeted diagnostic checks only where demonstrated failure modes justify them.

6. Revise through meaningful progress.

Each retry must:
- Inspect additional evidence.
- Correct a calculation.
- Repair a citation.
- Remove an unsupported claim.
- Or narrow the answer appropriately.

Rephrasing the same unsupported assertion until it receives approval is not progress.

Decisions provides a routing judgment, not a written critique. The reasoning model identifies the correction using original evidence and concrete validation failures.

A wrong room count can be corrected. An actual ceiling height absent from the supplied material cannot be recovered through repeated reasoning.

7. Publish with validated associations.

Show the answer, citations, limitations and reliably associated highlights.

Uncertain object mappings retain source evidence without invented highlights. A missing highlight must not suppress an otherwise supported textual answer.

If reconstruction changed during the request, revalidate highlight associations against the displayed revision. Original source citations remain available even if an earlier object mapping no longer works.

During Q&A, show progress such as:
- “Inspecting source.”
- “Checking answer.”

The model remains usable while the answer is prepared. Questions do not automatically trigger reconstruction.

SHARED EVIDENCE BOUNDARIES

- Original IFC records support answers about the supplied model; they are not proof of as-built reality.
- Drawing-derived IFC remains an interpretation, including after export and reopening.
- Unknown scale stays explicitly unscaled.
- Extrusion heights, decorative materials and proposed furnishings remain assumptions.
- Actual-height questions still refuse when the original source supplies no height.
- Concept additions never become factual evidence merely because they are visible.
- API failures are operational errors, not evidence-quality judgments.
- Missing information is scoped to the inspected material.
- Optional similar-building ideas remain explicitly hypothetical proposals.
- A reviewer’s approval is corroboration, not proof of correctness.
- Model confidence must not be presented as measured accuracy on this dataset.
- Dataset ground-truth answers remain evaluation-only and never become runtime context.

INTEGRATE THE EXISTING CONCEPT PRESENTATION

Inspect:

/home/jcb/dev/github/JunctionHack26-concept

Read its docs/CONCEPT_VISUALIZATION.md, inspect the implementation, verification artifacts and actual git state.

Reuse its existing Three.js concept layer. Keep the simpler inspection mode as the evidence-oriented view.

Do not build a replacement concept renderer or add Blender, remote rendering, new rendering services or downloaded asset libraries for this goal.

The concept worktree reportedly contains:

Its prior verification is useful context, not proof that it works with the current main-thread implementation.

Identify the presentation-specific changes and integrate them carefully. Do not replace newer reconstruction, provenance, scaling, opening, schematic geometry or QA fixes with the concept worktree’s older baseline.

Preserve unrelated work and inspect uncommitted changes before integrating anything.

Add immutable revision `user_values` records with ID, scope `{floor_id?,object_id?}`, property, typed value/unit, provenance `user_provided`, optional original evidence/source document ref, reason, base revision and submission identity. Shared assumption rows are computed/grouped by scope+property; distinguish `observed`, `inferred`, `display_assumption`, `unknown`, `user_provided` without changing observed source facts in place. A supplied height never calibrates XY. With unknown horizontal scale, retain the actual supplied height and unit for attributed QA, keep the scene unscaled, and disclose the separate display conversion used for vertical presentation; never treat relative plan units as metres.

`GET /api/buildings/{id}/assumptions` returns grouped rows and editable property descriptors. `POST /api/buildings/{id}/refinements` accepts `{base_revision_id, edits:[...], supporting_source_ids?:[...]}` and returns a job. Validate finite values, supported unit dimensions, scope, source refs and revision before publication; reject executable/arbitrary paths. Supported properties cover storey display/known height, source-referenced plan calibration, stair connectivity and source-linked interpretation corrections through typed patches. Ambiguous corrections remain reviewable inputs, not assumed facts. Do not silently ignore unsupported properties.

Apply and refine persists submitted provenance, assesses source conflicts, changes affected deterministic geometry or uses bounded targeted model review where interpretation is required, then atomically publishes accepted updates. Failed candidates retain submitted values/diagnostics separately plus the prior usable revision. No call on editing/keystrokes. Existing artifact-size validation remains; if the portable artifact cannot contain these sources, report that export as unavailable while retaining the complete local bundle rather than exporting provenance loss. QA can use user values with explicit attribution for appropriate questions, but drawing-only height questions still refuse unsupported source facts.

### Geometry and viewer

Keep three transforms separate: original page→local floor plane, local floor→building placement/elevation, and viewer-only exploded spacing. Preserve frozen source frames and shared-page scale. Permit supported registration in an unscaled common page frame without asserting metres: matching stair/exterior anchors with inspected evidence can establish translation/rotation; never independently scale floors or equalize footprints. Cross-page scale uncertainty remains explicit. Add source-linked registration/stair relationships with status and provenance; unsupported registration stays schematic.

Generate real storey elevations from supported values or explicitly attributed display spacing in the appropriate display unit. Stacked mode retains them; exploded mode adds spacing. Stair connectivity can use a continuous schematic ramp/flight between established storeys while recording unknown rise/vertical dimensions. Preserve source footprints and the larger terrace; do not introduce a connection from similarity alone. Export/reopen retains base elevation, relation and provenance. Source overlays inverse-transform actual reopened geometry, including building placement, to original coordinates.

Native scene floors derive from supplied storeys/containment even when storeys have no geometry. Missing/ambiguous containment remains visible without inventing a floor. Replace cutaway boolean with 0–100 slider: each selected floor uses its base elevation and supported height, or labeled display reference. In all-floor mode apply the same percentage independently to each storey's reference; uncontained geometry uses an explicitly displayed scene-wide reference. Use clipping planes in inspection and concept modes; do not rescale walls or move openings. Preserve percent, floor, mode, camera and selections across revision swaps.

Investigate wall/opening failures using retained descriptions, host keys, source segments, signed wall bands, transforms and actual reopened meshes. Structured local consistency findings identify duplicate/conflicting hosts, contradictory floor/stair relations, invalid projections and missing geometry, with source refs; they guide source review, not automatic nearest-wall snapping. If actual tapered walls need a richer representation, add optional source footprint polygons to the existing wall record and deterministic extrusion/void logic, retaining segment/band compatibility. Use real source evidence to distinguish extraction error from generator/display error.

## Work packages and ownership

1. **Root integration/backend:** `app/documents.py`, `bundles.py`, `building.py`, `schemas.py`, `reasoning.py`, `source_context.py`, `jobs.py`, `main.py`, `provider.py`, `openai_provider.py`, `service.py`, `revisions.py`, `identities.py`; related backend tests and integration docs. Own source contracts/cache, extraction split, source refs, conversation/user values, safe diagnostics, prompt budgets and artifact version coordination. Freeze shared schema changes before assigning dependent work.
2. **Geometry/frontend implementer:** `app/ifc_generate.py`, `ifc_import.py`, `comparison.py`, `scene.py`, `ifc_artifact.py`, `artifact_schema.py`, `app/static/*` and explicitly assigned geometry/browser tests. Root supplies shared models; implementer coordinates additive scene/artifact fields before editing. Implement source-first UI, multi-file selection/add, chat, assumptions, native floors/cutaway, registration/elevations/stairs and evidence-preserving viewer swaps. Root may split sequential assignments if one agent would be overloaded; no overlapping edits.
3. **Dedicated formats implementer, isolated worktree:** new `app/source_formats.py`/adapter modules and format tests only, plus a documented small integration patch for `DocumentStore` dispatch (root applies it). Contract: `normalize_vector_source(data: bytes, filename: str, *, max_edge: int = 4096) -> {pages, metadata, warnings}`; pages are PIL images with source-local indices, and JSON metadata carries original-vector↔normalized affine, original document units, preserved text and DXF layer/entity references. Core ingestion owns destination persistence and content hashes. No provider/job/frontend/schema edits. Assess installed renderers/converters first. Dependencies proposed to root in `requirements.in`; root resolves lock. SVG first; DXF next; DWG only after verified conversion path. Integrate independently reviewed commits, never a wholesale worktree replacement.
4. **Independent planner/reviewers:** plan reviewer read-only; implementation reviewers read-only against changed paths and acceptance evidence. Reviewer must not review own implementation. Direct browser interaction, original overlays and reopened IFC checks are required, not screenshot-only agreement. At most two plan review rounds, then root resolves remaining scope/architecture disagreements; implementation blockers must be fixed or explicitly reported.

A. Freeze reviewed contracts, inspect current git state and retain reproducible baselines. Diagnose unchanged colorful-34 live at its actual failure stage; retain structured output privately. Record initial gate/draft/review trace for the door refusal. Begin formats track independently after source adapter interface is fixed.

Source additions/extraction are source successes regardless of geometry. Preserve runtime evidence access before JSON completes.

C. Implement chat/clarification and attributed user inputs against the shared contracts. Implement source-first/multi-file UI. In parallel where ownership permits, implement native floors/cutaway and geometry placement/stair/wall corrections based on the actual diagnoses. Persist portable provenance and exact reference transforms.

D. Integrate SVG, then DXF; explicitly report verified or unavailable DWG path. Run matching institute SVG/PDF comparison and fresh format inputs. Run held-out evaluations after meaningful schema/prompt/geometry/QA changes, promoting discovered failures to regressions and replacing their held-out slot with a different building.

E. Independent implementation and browser review; fix blockers and rerun affected checks. Run `bash scripts/test.sh` and `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`, integrated live Gemini/browser checks, restart/reupload tests, then update handoff/verification evidence and make focused milestone commits without pushes.
